Social security minister has been overseeing review designed to ‘humanise’ the system but Tories say it will lead to higher spending and fewer checks

Q: [From Ali Fortescue from Sky News] We have done an interview with Rishi Sunak who says he is very concerned about the rise of ethnonationalism, and particularly with the suggestion from Suella Braverman, Reform UK’s education spokesperson, that people of Asian heritage can’t be English. Do you agree with him about that, and are you going to do anything about it?

Farage replied:

I’m very worried about it and I think you can see with the online right, both in this country and America, some pretty extraordinary things being said that would have been unthinkable even a handful of years ago …

So, yes, there is a rise in ethnonationalism. I’ve fought this all my career. No one did more to beat the BNP than me.

I view it as an unwelcome debate and I don’t want to hear anything about it again. Is that clear?

I do not trust the Conservative party on this issue. I trusted them back in 2019. I felt it was the right thing to do. I will never trust them again. And there’s no evidence to suggest that many of millions of others should do so.
